commercial-saas.description: Commercial cloud/SaaS application accessed over a network

proprietary-distributed.description: Proprietary binary, container, mobile app, or on-prem software distribution

commercial-distributed.description: Commercial binary or on-prem software distribution

research-noncommercial.description: Non-commercial academic or scientific research environment

rules.explanation_template: Component '{name}' ({license}) is governed by a network copyleft license (AGPL-3.0/SSPL Section 13). Deploying or interacting with this component in a {distribution_type} environment triggers mandatory disclosure of the complete Corresponding Source code of the entire service or distributed application.
rules.remediation_template: Remove '{name}' immediately or replace it with a permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause) alternative{alternative_hint}. Isolating AGPL components behind an internal microservice may still trigger Section 13 network interaction obligations if user requests flow through it.
obligations: Disclose complete Corresponding Source code to all network/distributed users under AGPL-3.0
Or remove/replace the component prior to deployment

rules.explanation_template: Component '{name}' ({license}) is a strong copyleft dependency linked or bundled in a PROPRIETARY_DISTRIBUTED build. Distributing binaries, containers, or on-premise packages containing {license} code requires licensing the combined derivative work under {license} and providing full source code.
rules.remediation_template: Replace '{name}' with a permissive (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD) alternative{alternative_hint}, or obtain a commercial dual-license exception from the copyright holder.
obligations: Provide full source code and build installation scripts to recipients under GPL terms
Refrain from imposing proprietary EULA restrictions on the distributed binary

rules.explanation_template: Component/Model weight '{name}' ({license}) carries a strict Non-Commercial restriction. Using '{name}' for inference, fine-tuning, synthetic data generation, or production serving in a commercial context violates the license grant.
rules.remediation_template: Replace '{name}' with commercially permissive model weights or libraries (e.g., Apache-2.0 or MIT licensed weights){alternative_hint}, or negotiate a direct commercial license with the rights holder.
obligations: Prohibited from any commercial use, revenue-generating SaaS inference, or commercial product integration

rules.explanation_template: Model weight '{name}' ({license}) permits commercial use but enforces mandatory Responsible AI behavioral use-case restrictions (Attachment A), including prohibitions on biometric surveillance/identification, medical diagnosis or clinical advice, administration of justice, and generating disinformation. These restrictions must legally flow down to all downstream users.
rules.remediation_template: Audit your product features and Terms of Service to ensure '{name}' is not used for restricted Attachment A domains (biometrics, medical diagnosis, law enforcement), and include the mandatory OpenRAIL Use-Based Restrictions in your user-facing Terms of Service. If unrestricted weights are required, switch to an Apache-2.0 alternative{alternative_hint}.
obligations: Pass through OpenRAIL Attachment A Use-Based Restrictions in downstream Terms of Service / EULA
Ensure model is not used for medical diagnosis, biometric categorization, or law enforcement
Include OpenRAIL-M license notice and attribution in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

rules.explanation_template: Model weight '{name}' ({license}) imposes user-count and usage restrictions that require review against terms of service: (1) products or services exceeding 700 million Monthly Active Users (MAU) on the model release date require a separate commercial license from Meta; (2) mandatory 'Built with Llama' UI/documentation attribution; and (3) compliance with the Llama Acceptable Use Policy.
rules.remediation_template: Verify that company/product scale is below the 700M MAU threshold, display 'Built with Meta Llama' prominently in product UI and documentation, and enforce the Llama Acceptable Use Policy. Otherwise, replace '{name}' with an Apache-2.0 model{alternative_hint}.
obligations: Confirm Monthly Active Users (MAU) did not exceed 700M on model release date
Display 'Built with Meta Llama' prominently on websites, UI, and documentation
Include Meta Llama Community License Agreement in distributions and notices
Enforce Meta Acceptable Use Policy in downstream terms

rules.explanation_template: Model weight '{name}' ({license}) includes custom model rider and prohibited-use covenants that must be enforced in downstream applications and user agreements.
rules.remediation_template: Review the specific model rider and prohibited use policy for '{name}', incorporate required flow-down clauses into your Terms of Service, or switch to an Apache-2.0/MIT model{alternative_hint}.
obligations: Flow down prohibited use policy restrictions to end users
Include model license attribution notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

rules.explanation_template: Component '{name}' ({license}) is governed by a weak copyleft license. Modifications to '{name}' files/libraries must be released under {license}, and PROPRIETARY_DISTRIBUTED builds using LGPL libraries must use dynamic linking (allowing users to relink modified versions of the library).
rules.remediation_template: Ensure '{name}' is dynamically linked without direct source modification, document dynamic linking compliance, and include {license} notices in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
obligations: Link LGPL libraries dynamically (no static binary linking without object files)
Disclose source code for any direct file-level modifications to the component
Include copyright and license text in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

rules.explanation_template: Component '{name}' ({license}) is a strong copyleft package used in a SAAS_HOSTED deployment. While standard GPL (unlike AGPL) is not triggered by pure backend network interaction, bundling '{name}' into downloadable client assets (e.g., frontend JS bundles, CLI agents, or SDKs) will trigger full copyleft source disclosure.
rules.remediation_template: Verify '{name}' runs strictly on backend servers and is never shipped to client browsers, mobile apps, or on-premise appliances. Consider replacing with a permissive alternative{alternative_hint}.
obligations: Keep component strictly server-side; do not bundle into client-facing downloads or JS bundles

rules.explanation_template: Component '{name}' has an unverified or proprietary license ('{raw_license}'). Under copyright law, absence of an explicit license grants no rights to use, modify, or distribute the software or model weights.
rules.remediation_template: Inspect the upstream repository or model card for '{name}' to verify its license terms, or replace it with a component carrying a verified SPDX/ML license.
obligations: Manually verify upstream license grant before production deployment

rules.explanation_template: Component '{name}' ({license}) is permissively licensed and compatible with {distribution_type} deployments provided standard copyright and attribution notices are retained.
rules.remediation_template: No remediation required. Retain attribution notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
obligations: Retain copyright notice and license text in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

inter_license_conflicts.explanation: Patent Clause Friction detected between Apache-2.0 ({components_a}) and GPL-2.0-only ({components_b}). Apache License 2.0 Section 3 includes patent litigation termination and indemnification provisions that the Free Software Foundation considers incompatible additional restrictions under GPL-2.0-only (Section 6).
inter_license_conflicts.remediation: Upgrade GPL-2.0-only component(s) ({components_b}) to 'GPL-2.0-or-later' / 'GPL-3.0' (which is compatible with Apache-2.0 patent clauses), or replace the GPL-2.0-only dependency with an Apache-2.0/MIT alternative.

recommended_alternatives.stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0: an Apache-2.0 licensed image generation model (e.g., 'black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell' under Apache-2.0)
